messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: alert detected: sustained increase in paged-kv metadata tags and block-manager lookup latency across prod-cluster-3. metric: kv_metadata_tags.total +220% over baseline in last 5m. affected: continuous-batching pipeline, several customer requests seeing >500ms p95 token latency. auto-pagebackoff triggered 3x.
amber (oncall): saw this spike too. customer-telemetry shows 2 customers with elevated error rates. throwing page eviction but metadata table still growing. marking P1 and paging SRE.
maya (eng-runtime): adding context: we rolled batch-window change yesterday (batch_window_ms: 20 -> 60) to reduce small-batch overhead. hypothesis: larger batch windows increase concurrent KV handles and cause metadata thrash + more block allocations.
kai (eng-runtime): confirmed correlation in traces — KV lookup counts per request doubled for long-context sessions after the change. block_manager.free_rate dropping.
leo (eng-sre): impact assessment: routing shows 15% latency cliff for gen-heavy routes, tail latency spikes causing timeouts to some webhooks. customers affected: "AtlasAI" and "Docsloop" (reported errors). recommending immediate partial rollback/canary to validate.
sarah (customer-success): pinged AtlasAI and Docsloop, both seeing intermittent 503s since 11:40. AtlasAI on a dedicated account asked for ETA. keeping them in the loop.
amber (oncall): plan proposal: 1) roll batch_window_ms back to 20 for 100% rollback OR 2) canary throttle: route 20% traffic to pre-change config while immediately enabling aggressive eviction and reduce max_block_size to limit metadata growth. prefer canary to avoid global rollback.
maya (eng-runtime): canary sounds good. quick mitigation steps I can push: - set eviction_scan_interval_ms: 500 -> 200 - set max_block_metadata_entries: 1_000_000 -> 250_000 - set max_block_size_bytes: 4_194_304 -> 2_097_152 - set continuous_batching.window_ms: 60 -> 30 (intermediate)
kai (eng-runtime): I'll prepare a canary route that sends 10% of traffic to the new config to validate rollback behavior before global. also we should disable the prefix KV caching for the canary to ensure observed metadata patterns are due to batch size not prefix blowup.
leo (eng-sre): throttle/route config sounds fine. add a metric alert: kv_metadata_tags.total_delta > +50% sustained for 3m -> paging escalation.
amber (oncall): set oncall note: timeboxed 45m. if canary doesn't reduce metadata growth within 10m, we roll full rollback to batch_window_ms:20.
sarah (customer-success): told AtlasAI: "we're deploying a canary fix now, expect intermittent retries around ~11:55, will update in 15m". they acknowledged.
maya (eng-runtime): deployment commands: ```
# canary config create
redwoodctl config apply --cluster prod-cluster-3 --path /configs/kv_block_manager/canary-176999 --set "eviction_scan_interval_ms=200" --set "max_block_metadata_entries=250000" --set "max_block_size_bytes=2097152" --set "continuous_batching.window_ms=30" --set "prefix_cache.enabled=false"
# route 10% traffic
redwoodctl route update --cluster prod-cluster-3 --route continuous-batching --canary-config canary-176999 --traffic-share 10
```
deploy-bot: deploy started for config canary-176999 on prod-cluster-3 (uid: dpl-176999-01). CI checks passed.
kai (eng-runtime): monitoring dashboards: created a short-lived overlay for canary with these metrics: kv_metadata_tags.total, block_lookup_latency.p95, continuous_batch_size.avg, eviction_cycles.per_min.
amber (oncall): initial canary metrics (T+2m): kv_metadata_tags delta down 18% on canary nodes vs baseline; block_lookup_latency.p95 improved ~120ms. not fully healed but trending.
leo (eng-sre): good sign. keep canary running 10m and then increase to 25% if stable. also prepare script for a fast full rollback: `redwoodctl config apply --cluster prod-cluster-3 --path /configs/continuous-batching --set "continuous_batching.window_ms=20"` with deploy-bot notify.
maya (eng-runtime): putting a temporary guard in the runtime to reject new large block allocations >2MB until we can do a controlled compaction. patch: ```diff
- if (block.size > MAX_BLOCK_SIZE) alloc()
+ if (block.size > RUNTIME_MAX_BLOCK_SIZE) return OOM_SAFE_ERROR
```
kai (eng-runtime): can we avoid a hard reject? worried about behavioral regressions. maybe return a soft-fail code that triggers fast eviction instead.
maya (eng-runtime): yeah will soft-fail and trigger immediate eviction sweep for the request. pushing patch to canary nodes only.
sarah (customer-success): AtlasAI says some calls improved after the canary deploy. Docsloop still seeing spikes, but they're lower frequency.
amber (oncall): timeline: canary T+10m complete. if stable, increase to 25%. keep CS updated every 15m. Amber -> escalate to platform lead if any customer reports >=2 minute outage.
leo (eng-sre): long term follow-ups: - investigate why metadata table growth isn't capped sooner (bug in metadata GC path) - add fuzz test for batch_window * prefix_cache interactions - add rollout-safe guard in autoscaler for block_manager memory usage
maya (eng-runtime): creating a PR for metadata GC fix and adding a unit test for stale tag cleanup. linking PR in thread.
amber (oncall): update: T+12m canary -> 25% traffic. metrics holding: kv_metadata growth flattened on canary, global cluster still high but trending down.
deploy-bot: canary scaled to 25% (uid: dpl-176999-02).
sarah (customer-success): AtlasAI confirms better, says will re-open if they see regressions. Docsloop asked for a postmortem and timeline; i'll coordinate.
leo (eng-sre): recommend post-incident follow-up doc with root cause: interaction of large batch_window + prefix_cache causing excessive per-request KV handle creation -> metadata leak and delayed GC. severity: P1. action owners set.
amber (oncall): closing the immediate P1 mitigation window. move to incident-review channel for postmortem. tagging @eng-rt-leads for follow-up. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: incident resolved on prod-cluster-3 at 1769990450. summary: canary throttle + eviction tuning reduced metadata growth and mitigated latency cliffs. further follow-ups scheduled.
